With Election Day set for Tuesday, November 3, the money race in the race for Texas' 28th Congressional District is running into the millions, according to the Laredo Morning Times. Democratic incumbent Henry Cuellar, who is seeking a 12th straight term, faces Republican nominee Tano Tijerina, the outgoing Webb County judge. Green Party candidate Marlon Duran did not raise or spend the $5,000 required to file campaign finance reports, the report says.

Tijerina's campaign reported $1,749,356.76 in disbursements through October 14, the Times reports — 71.9% of Cuellar's spending over the same period, which puts Cuellar's disbursements at roughly $2.43 million. Cuellar reported $3,043,039.01 in total receipts from January 1, 2025 through October 14, including $2,616,628.25 in contributions, $301,000 in loans and $112,198.08 transferred from committees. Tijerina reported $1,862,406.86 in receipts, or 61.2% of Cuellar's total.

The gap is even wider in the local state races, according to the Times. Three state incumbents — Democratic state Sen. Judith Zaffirini, Democratic state Rep. Richard Pena Raymond and state incumbent Don McLaughlin — together raised $3,219,679.05 against $52,606.64 for their challengers through October 24, and spent $3,196,745.30 against $144,759.58. The report puts the incumbents' share at 98.4% of receipts and 96.5% of disbursements in those races.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "Millions spent in D28 race, state incumbents account for over 98% of spending," October 31, 2026

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: The District 28 race is a multimillion-dollar contest: Tijerina reported about $1.75 million in spending through Oct. 14, while local state incumbents raised $3.22 million against just $52,607 for their challengers.
title: Millions in the District 28 race — and local state incumbents hold a near-total money edge
